target_customer: Web readers who clip and share pieces of content, plus bloggers and media sites that could add a snip widget for their readers
problem: Saving and sharing a piece of a web page meant copying and pasting; Snipd let users clip text, images or video with a bookmarklet and aggregated clips into heat maps of what readers cared about.
business_model: Free consumer clipping tool with planned monetization through publisher widgets and ads; a second TechCrunch piece discussed monetization plans

founders.name: Alex Schliker
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in TechCrunch coverage of the October 2008 public launch. The YC page lists no founders.

competitors.name: SimplyBox
competitors.what: Visual clipping tool shipped as browser plugins; snippets were images

competitors.name: Sazell
competitors.what: Web clipping service named by TechCrunch as a rival

competitors.name: Clipmarks
competitors.what: Clip paragraphs, sentences or multimedia from pages, with a source link

technical_complexity.rationale: A bookmarklet that captures a selection, stores it and renders a feed is modest engineering; preserving formatting and clipping streaming video added some difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Several clipping tools already existed and a bookmarklet is easy to copy; value depended on a user network that had not formed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer found; the YC directory lists the company as inactive and no source gives a date or cause.

market_need_then: Social bookmarking and clipping had several active products in 2007 and 2008, but a Hacker News launch thread contained user complaints about the highlight then click workflow, so need was unproven.

identity.voice_and_tone: Product language centered on a Snip It button and a Twitter for webclips pitch

branding.community_and_virality: Launch coverage on TechCrunch (October 2008) and a Hacker News thread; no merch or fan community found. A later, unrelated Swiss company of the same name (founded 2021) is not this company.

brand_strength.rationale: Only launch press found; the name was later reused by an unrelated podcast app, which shows the original brand left no lasting hold.

outcome_analysis: Snipd launched publicly in October 2008 from the Summer 2008 batch with a bookmarklet clipping tool and a hot zone idea, competing with SimplyBox, Sazell and Clipmarks. No funding amount, traction number, shutdown date or cause is public, so the cause of its inactive status is not public and no failure factors are asserted. The only commentary found is user criticism of the clipping workflow on launch day.
notes: YC lists no website for this company and no founders. Many search results about funding and operations concern an unrelated Zurich company called Snipd founded in 2021 (pre-seed around 700K dollars); none of that applies here. No funding for the 2008 company was found, which is unknown, not zero. Clipmarks is dated February 2007, more than a year before the batch, but is included as a pre existing rival.
